rows.title: Money Matters: Financial Literacy
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Complete a personal budget.
Utilize sources of information pertaining to personal savings and investment.

rows.title: American Sign Language I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will utilize American Sign Language to express and receive information about a variety of topics at a beginner level.
Students will demonstrate accuracy and proficiency in the use of learned structures and vocabulary.
Students will differentiate the unique cultural aspects of American Deaf culture from the unique cultural aspects of other cultures.

rows.title: Observation and Assessment for Early Learning and Development (DS3)
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Complete systematic observations and assessments of children’s development and learning using a variety of data collection methods to inform classroom teaching, environment design, interactions, and curriculum.
Evaluate the characteristics, strengths, limitations, and applications of contemporary observation and assessment tools.
Describe the ethical and professional responsibilities for educators in observing and assessing young children’s development and learning.

rows.title: Lifelong Understanding and Self-Development
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze their personal values, skills, and interests to increase self-awareness.
Understand the different educational options available.
Understand factors that influence health and well-being.
Use effective communication skills to interact with diverse populations.

rows.title: Advanced Composition
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: develop effective thesis statements and demonstrate competency in the use of specific rhetorical patterns and logical patterns of development in well-organized paragraphs and essays
analyze methods of support in academic essays and use similar methods in writing
paraphrase and summarize effectively
use primary and secondary sources effectively in a documented paper

rows.title: Biddle Physical Ability Test (PAT)
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate successful completion of all Physical Ability Test events without assistance with a passing score of 9 minutes and 34 seconds or less.

rows.title: Composition 1
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the four steps in the writing process
Demonstrate in writing 6 types of paragraphs including exemplification, compare/contrast, descriptive, cause and effect, process, and argument

rows.title: Multimedia Storytelling
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Report and construct news stories using a variety of media.
Identify and apply the legal and ethical responsibilities of the reporter.
Apply digital storytelling strategies across contemporary media platforms.

rows.title: Conditioning for Football
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Student will be able to differentiate between sport and position specific resistence training techniques that enable and or hinder football performance improvements.
Students will be competent at performing linear and non-linear football and position specific movements.

rows.title: Principles of Retailing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: develop the communication, information and reasoning skills necessary in the retail work environment to increase productivity and enhance career opportunities.
create hypotheses, compare and contrast possible problem solutions, analyze possible outcomes and recommend action plans in the ratail management business environment.

rows.title: Introduction to Pharmacy Technology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the duties and roles of the pharmacy technician in various practice settings.
Identify the skills needed to successfully complete the Pharmacy Technology program at SAC.
Summarize the license and certification process for pharmacy technicians.
Differentiate drugs classified as OTC, Rx, (federal legend) C1, C2, C3, C4, C5.
Identify the steps involved in new drug development.
Discuss the characteristics of common drug dosage forms.
Memorize the 100 common trade-generic equivalents and indications.
Interpret prescriptions, memorize prescription sig codes, and prepare prescription labels.

rows.title: Introduction to Communicative Disorders and Treatment
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic terminology related to the field of communicative disorders.
Demonstrate knowledge of the basic principles of evaluating and treating individuals with communication disorders.
